A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same filter-head study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original activation-patching experiments, head ablations, predicate-transfer evaluations, and concept-probing results for Llama-70B and Gemma-27B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds baseline accuracies, design-choice ablations, smaller-model experiments, and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: Sparse-mask head localization, query/key/residual interventions, predicate averaging and composition, SVD interventions, and the training-free probe remain unchanged. Renaming DCM to learned masks and specifying the optimization objective provide additional documentation without establishing a procedural revision.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix P.2 adds qualitative evaluations involving negation, logical deduction, divisibility, and odd-one-out selection. Appendix P.4 adds a product-review sentiment example. These modestly extend evaluated scenarios; the six systematic filtering tasks and existing language coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated head comparators, localization approaches, and Logit Lens probe baseline are retained. Concept and Induction heads are renamed Concept Induction and Token Induction, with unchanged comparisons. The additional model accuracy tables characterize studied models rather than introduce competing filtering methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds Llama-8B and Gemma-9B evaluations and baseline accuracy measurements on shared draws of 1024 examples. Appendix H introduces a controlled sparsity sweep using one-token patching without source averaging, plus separate one-token evaluations. These substantially extend the experimental design; the existing main evaluation protocol remains.

E4.justification: New Appendix H tests sensitivity to mask sparsity and patching only the final token, addressing two methodological choices. Appendix P adds generalization case studies and revises application examples. The composition and answer-free-source experiments newly summarized in Section 3.3 already existed in v1 Appendices D and E.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose that most causality scores come from one trial with 512 randomly sampled examples. V2 introduces no repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure. Its additional plus/minus logit entries follow reporting already present in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline, ablation, and smaller-model results, including object causality of 0.856 for Gemma-9B and 0.826 for Llama-8B in Table 15. Gemma portability values change from v1 Table 10 to v2 Table 14: English-to-English changes from 0.863 to 0.824, and question-before-to-before from 0.020 to 0.055. Main Llama-70B results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix H formally specifies the mask objective in Equation 7, including the mean competing-item logit and L1 penalty, where v1 provided a verbal objective description. Existing causal definitions and SVD reasoning are retained; the expanded matrix equality introduces no substantive derivation change.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: localized predicate representations, portability across contexts, and complementary lazy and eager filtering mechanisms. The discussion preserves these conclusions; additional experiments support their existing scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablation as showing that two-token patching is less critical than anticipated. Appendix M links weaker smaller-model transfer to possible representational entanglement. Section 4 adds a stronger interpretation about discarding unrelated context, while Appendix P expands discussion of generalization and alternative mechanisms in failure cases.

D1.justification: V2 supplies exact model checkpoint identifiers, the L1 objective and sparsity coefficient of 0.02, use of prior authors' datasets and code for head identification, and LLM assistance in dataset construction and translation. These are new disclosures, not established changes to existing implementations. Hardware and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Csordás et al. (2021) for differentiable masking and Vaswani et al. (2017) when discussing attention. It clarifies that other specialized heads test functional distinctiveness rather than serve as conventional task baselines. The main related-work section and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains a structured hypothesis, intervention setup, and results explanation drawing on existing Appendix B material. V2 also clarifies masking terminology, summarizes existing appendix findings in the main text, and polishes several passages. The overall narrative and main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with five new tables, the sparsity plot, smaller-model transfer heatmaps, and four additional qualitative task panels. Application visualizations are redrawn with different coloring and sentence-end borders. Most existing figures are retained and relocated, with smaller caption and labeling edits.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through design-choice ablations, smaller-model replication, and baseline accuracies. It also replaces v1's Gemma portability table, which duplicated Llama values, with model-specific results and improves reproducibility details. These provide an incremental net gain. Single-trial reporting persists, and the new Table 15 inconsistently states 47 Llama-8B heads in its caption versus 39 in the table and Figure 24.
